thesis: Causal explanation depends on mechanisms, alternatives and explicit assumptions, and does not itself allocate moral responsibility.
role: Shows how causal inference enables action without conflating association and intervention.

ideas.statement: Mechanism, enabling conditions and preventable intervention can all explain the same event.
Association cannot identify intervention effects without assumptions; aggregate patterns can reverse group patterns.
Causal explanation and moral accountability must be connected without being equated.

evidenceAndExamples.statement: The fictional training-course arithmetic shows aggregation reversal but proves neither benefit nor harm.

objectionsAndQualifications.statement: Bell results exclude a package of assumptions, not license arbitrary mystical claims; indefinite order retains constraints.

audit.notes: Read every unit; fictional examples and limits retained. Structural transitions excluded from ranking.
